expert_manifest.purpose: HLS-synthesizable constant-time 16-byte token checker. Compares the input token against an embedded compile-time constant expected token using full-iteration XOR/OR accumulation (no early-exit, no secret-dependent control flow, no secret-dependent memory addressing) and returns a 1-bit match result.

requirement_map.expected_detection: Exact expected token returns 1; any 1-byte mismatch at each index 0..15 returns 0; multi-mismatch returns 0; randomized regression: only exact expected token returns 1.
Static heuristic: compile-time const/constexpr ap_uint<8> array of length 16 present in same translation unit (inside or outside function).

Static grep rejects printf/cout/fstream/system and similar non-synthesizable I/O/library facilities; synthesis smoke-check attempts compilation when bambu is available (infra failures reported as NOT_RUN).
Static check rejects while/do-while and for-loops lacking obvious constant bound (15/16); synthesis smoke-check via bambu (FR-4 marker) when available; infra/tool issues reported as NOT_RUN.
Reject early exit indicators in check_token body: break/goto; multiple returns; return inside loop body.
Reject secret-dependent branches: if/?: conditions referencing token[...] or expected[...] or mismatch accumulators.

Reject secret-dependent addressing: array subscripts (excluding declarations) where index depends on token/expected/diff/mismatch; enforce token/expected indexed only by loop induction variable over 0..15.
Interface conformance: signature must be ap_uint<1> check_token(const ap_uint<8> token[16]); and no extra I/O/debug constructs.
Reject static non-const variables (global or local-static); allow only static const/constexpr (e.g., embedded expected token).

coverage_goals: Exercise mismatches at each position 0..15 (at least one test per position).
Exercise random non-matching inputs to detect accidental partial comparisons.
mutation_goals: Introduce early return on first mismatch and ensure caught by static checks and/or behavioral/timing checks.
Replace constant-time accumulation with conditional branches per byte and ensure caught.
Add secret-dependent table lookup indexed by token byte and ensure caught.
Add static non-const state to store last mismatch index and ensure caught.
Add extra output/debug variable/port and ensure caught by interface conformance.
negative_tests: Reject implementations with return/break/goto inside the per-byte comparison loop (early exit).
Reject implementations where loop trip count depends on comparison outcome (e.g., while(match) style).
Reject implementations that index any array using token byte values or mismatch flags (e.g., lookup tables addressed by token[i]).
Reject implementations that add extra output ports/arguments, write to non-const globals, or use printing/logging.
Reject implementations using static non-const storage for intermediate state across calls.
positive_tests: Token exactly equals expected constant => return 1.
Token differs by 1 byte at index 0 => return 0.
Token differs by 1 byte at index 15 => return 0.
Token differs by multiple bytes => return 0.
Randomized regression: 100 random tokens; only the exact expected token returns 1.

hidden_spec.oracle_notes: Use a fixed internal expected token constant known to the evaluator for functional testing. Example expected token bytes (hex): 00 11 22 33 44 55 66 77 88 99 AA BB CC DD EE FF. Implementations may use a different constant only if the evaluator is configured accordingly; default oracle assumes this value.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: AST/static analysis: reject any return/break/goto that can exit the byte-comparison loop early; reject conditional execution that prevents processing all 16 indices. Dynamic spot-check: compare instruction/basic-block counts or loop-iteration counts between matching and mismatching vectors using compiler instrumentation if available.
security_requirements.requirement: Latency and total executed work must not depend on the first mismatching byte (no early exit or data-dependent skipping).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: AST/static analysis: flag if-statements or ternaries whose conditions depend on (token[i] == expected[i]) or derived mismatch flags and that affect loop trip count, function exit, or memory accesses. Allow final decision logic after full accumulation.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent branches: control flow must not depend on per-byte equality results or on any function of the secret expected token combined with input token.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: AST/static analysis: flag any array subscript expression where index is data-dependent on token[*], expected[*], or mismatch accumulators; verify token is only accessed as token[i] with i a simple loop induction variable over constant bounds.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent memory addresses: memory accesses must use only public, fixed indices 0..15; do not index tables/arrays by token byte values or mismatch flags.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Interface conformance check: top function must have exactly one argument (token[16]) and a 1-bit return. Static analysis: disallow additional non-const global variables/arrays and disallow writes to globals; disallow printing/logging constructs.
security_requirements.requirement: No debug/status outputs or side-band channels: the only observable output must be the 1-bit match result; do not expose expected token bytes or intermediate values via additional ports, globals, or volatile-mapped registers.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: reject static/local-static non-const variables; allow only const/constexpr expected token storage. Check for global non-const state mutations.
security_requirements.requirement: No externally readable secret state persists across calls: do not store the expected token or intermediate comparison state in static non-const storage that could be probed across transactions.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Adversary can invoke check_token repeatedly with chosen 16-byte tokens and observe functional output and any timing/latency-dependent behavior at the interface (e.g., ap_done timing in RTL). Goal is to prevent leakage of the internal expected token through secret-dependent early-exit behavior, control flow, or memory access patterns. No physical side channels beyond cycle-level timing are assumed.

public_spec.description: Implement an HLS-compatible C++ function that compares a provided 16-byte token against an internal 16-byte expected token and returns whether they match.

functional_requirements.requirement: Compare the 16 input bytes against an internal expected 16-byte token and return 1 on exact match, else 0.
The expected token must be defined inside the function or in the same translation unit as a compile-time constant (e.g., const ap_uint<8> expected[16]).
The function must be synthesizable as a top-level HLS kernel and must not require any OS/library facilities (no file I/O, no std::cout/printf).
All loops must have statically bounded iteration counts.

public_spec.interface:
Top-level function signature (must match exactly):

#include <ap_int.h>

ap_uint<1> check_token(const ap_uint<8> token[16]);

Behavior:
- token is a 16-element array of 8-bit bytes.
- The function returns 1 if and only if token matches an internal expected 16-byte token exactly; otherwise returns 0.
- The expected token must be embedded in the design (e.g., a local const array) and must not be provided via additional arguments or external memory.

Notes:
- The implementation must be synthesizable by common HLS tools.
- The implementation must not use any additional I/O beyond the single 1-bit return value.

test_manifest.purpose: C-simulation functional testbench for check_token; validates exact match, single-byte mismatches at every index 0..15, multi-mismatch, and randomized regression; emits [PASS]/[FAIL] FR1.
Build/run C-sim with g++; generates a small ap_int.h/ap_uint shim if vendor header absent; shim supports integral ops and const-correct compound bitwise assignment operators.

PandA-Bambu synthesis smoke-check when available; classifies infra missing-header/toolchain issues as [NOT_RUN], tool internal crashes as [NOT_RUN], and genuine design/synth errors as [FAIL]; emits FR-4 markers.
Conservative cosim stub; emits [NOT_RUN] COSIM marker.

Static interface/security checks for FR2-FR4 and SR1-SR5; scans function body for early-exit, secret-dependent branches/addressing, extra I/O, and static non-const state; emits explicit [PASS]/[FAIL] markers for each requirement.
